summary: New Zealand: Investor 1 (NZ$10m, 2009-2022), Investor 2 (NZ$1.5m then NZ$3m, 2009-2022) and Active Investor Plus (2022; revamped April 2025 to NZ$5m Growth / NZ$10m Balanced) are covered from INZ's operational-manual instructions, MBIE Cabinet papers, INZ's residence-decision statistics (2013/14-2026/27) and a time series of INZ's AIP statistics page (April 2025-September 2026, with nationality, category and investment-type tables); demand jumped from 115 applications in 2.5 years to 949 in 18 months after the revamp. Australia: adds the Premium Investor visa (A$15m, 2015-2021), which official data show was barely used (one primary grant in the Migration Program data), plus Senate Estimates answers and Home Affairs FOI releases with Significant Investor and Investor stream lodgements, grants, refusal rates and Chinese/Hong Kong splits that wave 1 lacked.

programs.name: Investor 1 Category (Migrant Investment Policy)
programs.notes: Resident visa (permanent residence from the start, with conditions) for investing NZ$10 million in acceptable New Zealand investments for three years; no age, English or business-experience test. Investor had to spend a minimum time in New Zealand (73 days a year at first; from 2017, 44 days in each of the final two years, or 88 days over three years with NZ$2.5m in 'growth investments'). Created with Investor 2 by immigration instructions effective 27 July 2009; closed to new applications on 27 July 2022 (instructions shown 'to 28/07/2022') when Active Investor Plus replaced it; applications already lodged kept being processed (125 in progress in Dec 2023). Citizenship can follow through the ordinary residence route. Cabinet paper (2022): NZ$6.78bn initial investment and 679 investors over 13 years.

programs.name: Investor 2 Category (Migrant Investment Policy)
programs.notes: Points-based resident visa (expression of interest, then invitation to apply) for investors with business experience and English, investing NZ$1.5 million for four years (plus NZ$1 million settlement funds) from 27 July 2009, and NZ$3 million from 22 May 2017, when the settlement-funds rule was dropped and the annual cap rose from 300 to 400 approvals. Investor had to spend 146 days a year in New Zealand in the final three years (or 438 days over four years with 25% in growth investments, from 2017). Closed permanently to new applications on 27 July 2022; pipeline still processed (277 in progress in Dec 2023). Cabinet paper (2022): NZ$5.184bn initial investment and 2,385 investors since 2009.

programs.name: Active Investor Plus Visa (resident visa)
programs.notes: Resident visa for investors, run by Immigration New Zealand, with Invest New Zealand (formerly NZTE) deciding which funds and direct investments are acceptable. Opened 19 Sept 2022 with a NZ$15 million threshold or weighted equivalent (direct investment weighted 3x, so NZ$5 million minimum; listed equities capped at 50%, bonds and property excluded), 117 days in NZ over four years and an English requirement. Few applications under those settings (115 to 31 Mar 2025). Revamped from 1 April 2025: Growth category NZ$5 million for 3 years (managed funds, direct investment; 21 days in NZ) and Balanced category NZ$10 million for 5 years (adds bonds, listed equities, property development; 105 days); English requirement removed. Applications then rose sharply (949 by 24 Sep 2026; 496 approved, about NZ$2.88bn committed), led by US, Chinese and Hong Kong applicants. Build to Rent funds to be added to Growth from December 2026. Holders can apply for permanent residence after the investment period; citizenship through the ordinary residence route.

programs.name: Premium Investor visa: Premium Investor stream of the Business Innovation and Investment visa (subclass 188 provisional, 888 permanent)
programs.notes: By-invitation stream within aus-biip for people nominated by Austrade (no state nomination, no unsolicited expressions of interest) who made a complying premium investment of at least AUD15 million and held it for 12 months, after which they could apply for permanent residence (subclass 888 Premium Investor). Introduced 1 July 2015 alongside the revised Significant Investor rules; closed to new applications from 1 July 2021 after the BIIP review. Barely used: Home Affairs FOI releases show no applications or grants to 31 May 2017, fewer than five in 2018-19 and none from July 2019 to March 2020; the Migration Program data record a single primary grant (a Canadian national, 2018-19).

programs.name: Pre-2012 Business Skills investor visas: Investor (Provisional) subclass 162, State/Territory Sponsored Investor (Provisional) subclass 165, State/Territory Sponsored Business Investor (Residence) subclass 893
programs.notes: Investor visas of the Business Skills programme (first version established in 1992, per a 2016 Home Affairs FOI release), replaced by the Business Innovation and Investment Program (aus-biip) from 1 July 2012; the provisional visas are closed to most new applications (family members can still be added). Applicants made a 'designated investment' (state or territory government bonds) for four years, then could apply for permanent residence (892/893). Investment thresholds over time not yet sourced. Only tail-end grants appear in the Migration Program data from 2015-16.
